description: On a runner with Docker and systemd: report mode changes nothing; apply adds log rotation and build-cache limits to daemon.json without disturbing the keys already there, writes a file dockerd accepts, and makes nothing that belongs to Docker - Configure Host Maintenance [Lin] (no list, prune, timer or state directory); a second run changes nothing; with all the limits blank the file is not touched; bad input is refused with exit 2 before anything is written. Docker stopped (docker.service stopped, docker.socket still listening): Report and Apply do not read Docker's start flags (exit 3) and leave docker.service inactive. With Docker restarted under extra daemon flags each time: a --log-driver=journald daemon and a --log-opt daemon get no log-opts in daemon.json and still start; a --log-driver=json-file daemon gets them and starts with them; a stopped daemon's flags are not worked out from docker.service: log rotation is skipped with exit 3, build-cache limits are still added, Docker starts with the file, and the next run with Docker running finishes the job (it skips log rotation for a journald daemon, and adds it for a daemon with no logging flag); a daemon started with --config-file pointing at another file gets nothing written to either file, exit 3; a daemon.json an earlier version already broke is reported as DAEMON WILL NOT START, exit 3, unchanged, and Docker really does fail to start with it. Writing daemon.json: the new file is made in the directory of the real target and renamed into place, so it keeps the mode, owner and group of the file it replaces (a 0600 file holding a fake proxy credential stays 0600 with its non-root group; a new file is 0644 root:root) and a symlinked daemon.json stays a symlink while its target changes and Docker restarts with it; a dangling symlink, or a link to a directory, is refused with exit 3 and nothing is created; after a successful Apply, a failed validation and Report mode, no .daemon.json.tc-* file is left in /etc/docker, and one left by a crashed earlier run is removed; Report mode on a host with no /etc/docker does not create it; seven changes in a row leave the newest five backups; and an immutable daemon.json makes the run exit 1 with the file byte-for-byte unchanged, no staging file and no backup. Restarting Docker to load the new settings, and a host without Docker, are Tier 2. The script's opening comment is short and points to the README (a step reads it). These steps were in Docker - Configure Host Maintenance [Lin]'s spec up to its version 14, when this code was part of that component.

steps.label: Header: the script's opening comment is short (what it is, what it changes on the host, its exit codes) and points to the README, which holds the rest
steps.run: f=Scripts/docker-configure-daemon-limits-lin/docker-configure-daemon-limits-lin.sh; [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "cannot find $f from $(pwd)"; exit 1; }; n=$(awk 'NR > 1 && /^#/ { n++; next } NR > 1 { exit } END { print n + 0 }' "$f"); echo "header comment: $n lines"; [ "$n" -ge 10 ] && [ "$n" -le 35 ] && echo 'header is 35 lines or fewer'; h() { awk 'NR > 1 && /^#/ { print; next } NR > 1 { exit }' "$f"; }; echo "says what it changes: $(h | grep -c '^# Changes on the host')"; echo "points to its README: $(h | grep -c '^# https://github.com/TechCollective/DattoRMM_Components/tree/main/Scripts/docker-configure-daemon-limits-lin$')"; echo "exit codes: $(h | grep -c '^# Exit codes:$')"

outputContains: daemon.json: REPORT MODE, would write the change above

daemon.json carries the limits
Every key that was already there is unchanged
steps.run: python3 -c "import json,sys; a=json.load(open('/tmp/tc-before.json')); b=json.load(open('/etc/docker/daemon.json')); bad=[k for k in a if b.get(k)!=a[k] and k not in ('log-opts','builder')]; print('changed:', bad); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)"

steps.label: dockerd accepts the new file

steps.label: Daemon flags: set up a helper that restarts Docker with extra dockerd flags through a docker.service drop-in
steps.run: set -e; systemctl show docker.service -p ExecStart --value | sed -n 's/.*argv\[\]=\([^;]*\) ;.*/\1/p' | head -n 1 > /tmp/tc-execstart; test -s /tmp/tc-execstart; printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# tc-test-docker-flags FLAG...: restart docker.service with these extra dockerd flags (a drop-in).' 'd=/etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d' 'mkdir -p "$d"' '{ echo "[Service]"; echo "ExecStart="; echo "ExecStart=$(cat /tmp/tc-execstart) $*"; } > "$d/tc-test.conf"' 'systemctl daemon-reload' 'systemctl reset-failed docker.service docker.socket 2>/dev/null' 'if systemctl restart docker.service; then' '  for i in $(seq 30); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done' '  echo "docker came up with [$*]: LoggingDriver=$(docker info --format "{{.LoggingDriver}}")"' 'else' '  echo "docker DID NOT START with [$*]"' '  journalctl -u docker.service -n 50 --no-pager | grep -E "failed to start|unable to configure|unknown log opt|specified both" | tail -n 3' '  exit 1' 'fi' > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-docker-flags; chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-docker-flags; echo "docker.service starts: $(cat /tmp/tc-execstart)"

steps.label: daemon.json write: install a helper that runs the component several times inside one step
steps.run:
cat > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-run-component <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-run-component [VAR=value ...]: run the component body the way the harness does (root, clean environment, the script's own defaults), for a step that needs several runs.
exec env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin HOME=/root "\$@" /bin/bash "$(pwd)/Scripts/docker-configure-daemon-limits-lin/docker-configure-daemon-limits-lin.sh"
EOF
chmod 755 /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-run-component; echo "helper runs: $(grep -c exec /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-run-component) exec line"

steps.label: daemon.json write: seven changes in a row, each made by a run of the component
steps.run:
set -u
rm -rf /opt/tc-test-managed; rm -f /etc/docker/daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* /etc/docker/.daemon.json.tc-*; mkdir -p /etc/docker
printf '{"debug": false}\n' > /etc/docker/daemon.json
: > /tmp/tc-bak-names
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do
  python3 -c "import json; p='/etc/docker/daemon.json'; d=json.load(open(p)); d.pop('log-opts', None); d.pop('builder', None); json.dump(d, open(p, 'w'))"
  tc-test-run-component > /tmp/tc-run.out 2>&1 || { echo "change $i failed"; cat /tmp/tc-run.out; exit 1; }
  grep -q 'daemon.json: written' /tmp/tc-run.out || { echo "change $i wrote nothing"; cat /tmp/tc-run.out; exit 1; }
  LC_ALL=C ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* | tail -n 1 >> /tmp/tc-bak-names
done
echo "newest backup after each change:"; sed 's|^/etc/docker/||' /tmp/tc-bak-names
echo "backups after seven changes: $(ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* | wc -l)"
echo "distinct backup names made: $(sort -u /tmp/tc-bak-names | wc -l)"
diff <(LC_ALL=C ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-*) <(LC_ALL=C sort /tmp/tc-bak-names | tail -n 5) && echo "the five left are the newest five"
ls -la /etc/docker
outputContains: the five left are the newest five

steps.label: daemon.json write: an immutable daemon.json (chattr +i; skipped where the filesystem cannot): exit 1, file unchanged, no staging file, no backup
steps.run:
rm -rf /opt/tc-test-managed; rm -f /etc/docker/daemon.json /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* /etc/docker/.daemon.json.tc-*; mkdir -p /etc/docker
p=/etc/docker/.tc-immutable-probe; : > $p
if ! chattr +i $p 2>/dev/null || ! lsattr $p 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' | grep -q i; then
  chattr -i $p 2>/dev/null; rm -f $p
  echo "SKIPPED: this filesystem does not support chattr +i, so the immutable-file check did not run"; exit 0
fi
chattr -i $p; rm -f $p
f=/etc/docker/daemon.json
printf '%s\n' '{"proxies": {"http-proxy": "http://tc-test-user:tc-test-not-a-password@proxy.invalid:3128"}}' > $f; chmod 600 $f; chattr +i $f
sha256sum $f > /tmp/tc-imm.before
tc-test-run-component > /tmp/tc-imm.out 2>&1; rc=$?
chattr -i $f
cat /tmp/tc-imm.out
echo "component exit: $rc"
ok=0
[ "$rc" = 1 ] || { echo "WRONG: expected exit 1"; ok=1; }
grep -q "could not replace $f" /tmp/tc-imm.out || { echo "WRONG: the output does not say what failed"; ok=1; }
sha256sum -c /tmp/tc-imm.before || { echo "WRONG: daemon.json changed"; ok=1; }
n=$(ls -A /etc/docker | grep -c '^\.daemon\.json\.tc-' || true); echo "staging files left in /etc/docker: $n"; [ "$n" = 0 ] || ok=1
b=$(ls /etc/docker/daemon.json.tc-bak-* 2>/dev/null | wc -l); echo "backups left by the failed run: $b"; [ "$b" = 0 ] || ok=1
ls -la /etc/docker
exit $ok
